On each segment, the port advertising the best root information becomes the **designated port**. With the same root ID, compare root path cost, then sender bridge ID and sender port ID. Root and designated ports forward data once the relevant state transitions have completed; a role alone does not imply immediate forwarding. [nf-stp-port-roles.md]

In this stable classic-STP example, an enabled redundant port that is neither root nor designated is **blocked**: it still listens to BPDUs but forwards no data. During convergence, even a root or designated port can temporarily be listening or learning. [nf-stp-port-roles.md]

The fix is **pipelining**: permit several frames to be outstanding (sent but not yet acknowledged). Use a loss-free fixed-frame model with no queueing, processing, ACK transmission or framing gaps. The formula defines the window size below. [nf-window-pipeline.md]

Sustained offered traffic above a link’s service rate causes backlog or drops. High average utilisation can increase delay, but a utilisation number alone does not establish the queue state. [network-congestion]

Sending data again after loss, damage or an acknowledgement timeout. A successful retransmission can deliver previously missing useful data; goodput counts those bytes once, while all extra attempts consume capacity. [retransmission]
For a completed transfer with equal payload sizes, if 5% of attempts are extra retransmissions, unique delivered payload accounts for 95% of attempted payload. [retransmission]

A component coupling changing magnetic flux between windings to transfer electrical energy or signals. Separate, appropriately insulated windings can provide galvanic isolation; an autotransformer has a shared winding and does not. [transformer-electrical]
Ethernet magnetics can isolate the cable-side circuitry from equipment-side circuitry; the actual part and circuit determine isolation ratings. [transformer-electrical]

A component storing energy in an electric field. In a series coupling path it passes changing signal components while blocking steady current after charging; actual frequency response depends on capacitance and the surrounding circuit. [capacitor]

Fiber Distributed Data Interface: a 100 Mbit/s token-passing fibre LAN standard using a dual-ring architecture and 4B/5B coding. Fast Ethernet also uses 4B/5B in particular PHYs; this entry makes no claim that all fibre networks use FDDI. [fddi]

A classic-STP port in the blocking state receives relevant BPDUs but does not forward user data or learn source addresses. In a stable simple topology this includes redundant enabled ports outside the root/designated forwarding set; role and state are distinct during convergence. [blocked-port]
With the stated 1500-byte frames, 1 Gbit/s link and 30 ms propagation round trip, stop-and-wait utilisation is about 0.04%, ignoring ACK time and other overhead. [stop-and-wait]
In the loss-free 1 Gbit/s model with 1500-byte frames and 30 ms propagation round trip, a 2501-frame window covers the full frame-plus-feedback cycle. [outstanding-frames]

The textbook alternating-bit stop-and-wait model uses a one-bit sequence number, with suitable ordering and packet-lifetime assumptions; arbitrary old duplicates cannot be handled by finite numbering alone. [sequence-number]

100BASE-TX is a 100 Mbit/s Fast Ethernet PHY over two twisted pairs, using 4B/5B and MLT-3 at 125 million symbol intervals per second. Fast Ethernet also includes other PHYs, so the family name is not synonymous with this one variant. [fast-ethernet]
Fast Ethernet is a PHY family, not an alias exclusively for 100BASE-TX. [fast-ethernet-family]

A Gigabit Ethernet coding/PHY family using 8b/10b at 1.25 gigabaud. It includes optical variants such as 1000BASE-SX and 1000BASE-LX and the short-reach copper 1000BASE-CX variant; not every member uses fibre. [1000base-x]
